title: UK labour market overview — earnings, unemployment and vacancies (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET), the last wage read inside the November Monetary Policy Report's data set
source: EST: two publisher primaries fetched direct 2026-09-09, both HTTP 200. (1) ons.gov.uk/releases/uklabourmarketoctober2026 — the ONS release-calendar entry reads verbatim 'UK Labour Market: October 2026', '20 October 2026 7:00am', 'Estimates of employment, unemployment, inactivity, average weekly earnings, vacancies and other labour market related statistics for the UK', marked 'This release is not yet published.' (2) gov.uk/government/statistics/announcements/uk-labour-market-october-2026 — the UK's statutory pre-announcement register reads verbatim '20 October 2026 7:00am (confirmed)', producer Office for National Statistics. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts carries BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS:/FED: and no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics — the same gap uk-labour-market-2026-09-15 was filed under. The DATE is not in doubt; the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Proposed 2026-09-09 by both the boe-decision-2026-11-05 and uk-labour-market-2026-09-15 lanes; researched and made canonical by its own lane the same day
notes: RESEARCHED 2026-09-09 by its own lane (docs/research/events/uk-labour-market-2026-10-20.md), which read both proposals in full and re-fetched every primary rather than inheriting them. The two proposals it supersedes — proposals/uk-labour-market-2026-10-20.from-boe-decision-2026-11-05.json and proposals/uk-labour-market-2026-10-20.from-uk-labour-market-2026-09-15.json — are now inert and stay where they are. TITLE AMENDED, and the amendment is this entry's finding. Both proposals filed it as 'the last wage read before the Autumn Budget'. That framing is calendar-true and forecast-false: the OBR's economy forecast for the 2026-10-28 EFO closes weeks before Budget day (its own published timetables put the initial economy forecast with the Treasury on 2025-09-17 for a 2025-11-26 Budget and on 2026-01-14 for a 2026-03-03 statement), so a print landing D-8 cannot be in it. What the print IS inside is the BANK's data set: the November 2025 MPR's data cut-off was 2025-10-28 for a 2025-11-06 publication and the February 2026 MPR averaged energy prices to 2026-01-26 for a 2026-02-05 publication — 9 and 10 days — which puts a 2026-11-05 cut-off around 2026-10-26/27 and this print 6-7 days inside it. IMPACT LOW, AND ARGUED RATHER THAN INHERITED: symbols [], this repo tracks no UK-listed symbol and no house playbook is rates- or sterling-keyed; the measured reaction to the last release was ~0.1% in cable on a two-sided beat. The one operational note that IS ours: on 2026-10-20 the 07:00 London / 02:00 ET print is the first macro release of the ET session by 6.5 hours (housing-starts-2026-10-20 at 08:30 ET, pending-home-sales-2026-10-20 at 10:00 ET) and the FOMC blackout has been running since 2026-10-17, so a pre-dawn gilt or cable move that morning has one candidate explanation. That discipline does NOT survive to the next morning: uk-cpi-2026-10-21 and the UK public sector finances release share the same 07:00 London minute on 2026-10-21. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
